mainTopic: Whether a גט may be written on a living creature, how each side reads the פסוקים about גט, and the dispute over a partition whose gaps equal its built parts (פרוץ כעומד).
overview: This amud has two topics. First it finishes the משנה about using a living creature for halachic purposes. רבי מאיר says a living גולל is טהור, and רבי יוסי הגלילי says a גט written on a living thing is פסול. A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the word 'ספר' that a גט must be written on something that is not alive and not food. The רבנן read 'ספר' as 'ספירות דברים', the content of the גט, so for them any material works. The גמרא then traces which words each side uses for two shared rules: a divorce happens only by writing and not by money, and a גט must fully cut the bond between husband and wife. Next, a new משנה teaches that a caravan may fence itself in with animal gear and carry inside, as long as the gaps are not more than the built parts and no single gap is wider than ten אמות. רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע argue about a fence whose gaps exactly equal its built parts (פרוץ כעומד). The wording of the משנה poses a קשיא for רב הונא, a proof from a סוכה roofed with skewers is pushed aside, and a new proof from a ברייתא about a caravan begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר rules a living גולל is pure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה records רבי מאיר's opinion that a living creature used as a grave covering does not carry the טומאה of a גולל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר says it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of the משנה. The first opinion said a living creature used to cover a grave becomes טמא like a גולל, and רבי מאיר disagrees and says it stays טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה treats a living creature like any other object, so it can be a לחי and can even get the status of a גולל. רבי מאיר holds that a living thing cannot fill these roles at all. Because it is not a real גולל, it does not carry גולל-טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules something pure (טהור)
The covering stone of a grave, which carries טומאה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir deems it pure.
phrases.notes: This is about a living creature used to cover a grave (a גולל).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf about a living creature used as a לחי and as a גולל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a living creature used as a גולל does not transmit גולל-טומאה.

steps.title: Writing a גט on a living creature
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a גט may be written on a living creature, but רבי יוסי הגלילי says such a גט is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may write women's גיטין on it, but רבי יוסי הגלילי says it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more use of a living creature: you may write a גט on it. רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees and says a גט written on a living thing is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, the material of a גט, but it uses the same idea of whether a living thing counts as a valid object. The first opinion says yes. רבי יוסי הגלילי says no, and the גמרא will soon ask for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: Bills of divorce given to women
Rules something invalid

phrases.english: And one may write women's bills of divorce on it,
but Rabbi Yosei HaGelili invalidates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second dispute to the משנה, this time about a גט instead of a גולל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion says a גט written on a living creature is valid. רבי יוסי הגלילי says it is invalid.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי מאיר's list of things a living creature cannot be
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives רבי מאיר's full list: a living thing cannot be a סוכה wall, a לחי, a פס around a well, or a גולל. In the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי, it cannot be used for a גט either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר says that anything alive may not be made into a wall for a סוכה, a לחי for a מבוי, boards around wells, or a cover for a grave. In the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי they said: one also may not write a גט on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that spells out רבי מאיר's view more fully than the משנה did. It also adds רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling about a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only mentioned the לחי and the גולל. The ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר has one general rule: a living thing is never a valid halachic structure, whether for a סוכה, a מבוי, wells, or graves. רבי יוסי הגלילי extends the same exclusion to the material of a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: The breath of life; a living creature
A wall of a סוכה
A side post that makes an alleyway usable on שבת
Upright boards around a well, used on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions here. רבי מאיר's list covers walls, side posts, boards, and the גולל. Only the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי is attached to the גט ruling.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a baraita,
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים
phrases.english: Anything that has the breath of life in it

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ לֹא דּוֹפֶן לְסוּכָּה
phrases.english: may not be made into a wall for a sukka,
nor a side post for an alleyway,
nor boards for wells,
nor a covering for a grave.
In the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili they said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵין כּוֹתְבִין עָלָיו גִּיטֵּי נָשִׁים.
phrases.english: Also, one may not write women's bills of divorce on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that gives the fuller version of the opinions in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a living thing is invalid as a סוכה wall, לחי, פס, or גולל. רבי יוסי הגלילי: a גט may not be written on it either.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling that a גט cannot be written on a living thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי הגלילי invalidates a גט written on a living creature. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on his view. It is a request for its source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק or logic tells us that the material of a גט cannot be alive.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the רבי יוסי הגלילי ruling quoted in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a גט cannot be written on a living creature.

steps.title: ברייתא: a גט must be like a scroll, not alive and not food
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'וכתב לה' that a גט can be written on anything. It then uses the word 'ספר' to limit this: like a scroll, the material must not be alive and must not be food.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'ספר' would teach only a scroll. From where do we include anything else? The פסוק says 'וכתב לה,' meaning on anything. If so, why does it say 'ספר'? To tell you: just as a scroll is not alive and is not food, so too a גט may be written on anything that is not alive and not food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about גט very carefully. The result is that a גט may not be written on something living or on food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three moves. First, the word 'ספר' alone suggests only an actual scroll. Second, 'וכתב לה' widens this to any material. Third, 'ספר' is still needed, so it narrows the rule back to materials that share a scroll's features: not alive and not food. That is exactly why רבי יוסי הגלילי invalidates a גט written on a living creature.

keyTerms.meaning: A scroll or document (from the פסוק about גט, דברים כ״ד:א׳)
From where do we include?
The פסוק says (introduces a proof from a verse)
And he shall write for her
Just as... so too (a comparison pattern)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the word 'ספר' sets the rule for the material of a גט: it must be something that is neither alive nor food.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
From "scroll," I would have only a scroll.
From where do we include any object?
The verse says "and he shall write for her," meaning on anything.
If so, why does the verse say "scroll"?
To tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה סֵפֶר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים
phrases.english: just as a scroll is something that has no life in it
and is not food,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֶל.
phrases.english: so too, anything that has no life in it and is not food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by bringing a ברייתא that reads the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'ספר' limits the material of a גט to something like a scroll: not alive and not food.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: one word seems to limit, a second phrase widens the rule, and then the first word is reused to define the scope by comparison ('מה ספר... אף').

steps.title: How do the רבנן read the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who allow a גט on a living creature, deal with the word 'ספר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the word 'ספר,' since they allow a גט on a living thing. This sets up the next step, which gives their reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ספר' really limits the material of a גט, the רבנן would seem to be going against the פסוק. So the גמרא needs to show how they explain the word in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages (the majority opinion): how do they explain it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The question is: what do the Rabbis do with this way of learning it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יוסי הגלילי's derivation to the opposing view of the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן explain the word 'ספר' if it does not limit the material of a גט.

steps.title: The רבנן: 'ספר' means the content, not the material
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן point out that the פסוק does not say 'בספר' (in a scroll). It says 'ספר,' which they read as 'ספירות דברים,' an account of the matters, meaning the text of the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'בספר' (in a scroll)? It is written 'ספר,' which comes only to teach an account of the matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer. 'ספר' is not about what the גט is written on. It is about what the גט says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah had written 'בספר,' with the letter ב meaning 'in,' it would describe the surface the גט is written on. Since it just says 'ספר,' the רבנן connect it to 'ספירה,' an account or statement of words. So the word teaches that a גט needs proper content, and it puts no limit on the material, so a living creature is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? (a rhetorical question, implying it is not)
In a scroll
An account of the matters; the text or content of the document
Merely, simply

steps.whatToRemember: The whole dispute rests on one word. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads 'ספר' as describing the material of the גט, so it cannot be alive or food. The רבנן read it as 'ספירות דברים,' the content of the גט, so any material is fine.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן ignore the word 'ספר.' They learn something from it, but they apply it to what the גט says rather than to what it is written on.

phrases.english: Is it written "in a scroll"?
"Scroll" is written,
and it comes merely to teach an account of the matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by giving the רבנן's different reading of 'ספר.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ספר' without a ב refers to the content of the גט (ספירות דברים), not to the writing surface.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the רבנן allow a גט on any material, even a living creature or food. It also shows how a single letter (ב) can change a whole דרשה.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from 'וכתב לה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the words 'וכתב לה', since they do not use them to allow a גט on anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they learn from this phrase 'and he shall write for her'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the רבנן. This sets up the next step, where we will see what they learn from 'וכתב לה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי הגלילי needed 'וכתב לה' to widen the rule beyond an actual scroll. For the רבנן, 'ספר' never limited the material in the first place (step 7), so they do not need 'וכתב לה' to widen anything. The גמרא assumes every word of the תורה teaches something, so it asks what job 'וכתב לה' does for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis (the majority view that argues on רבי יוסי הגלילי)
'And he shall write for her', the words of the פסוק about a גט
What do they learn (expound) from it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this phrase 'and he shall write for her'
what do they learn from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how the רבנן read 'ספר', the גמרא asks how they use the other phrase, 'וכתב לה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the רבנן learn from the phrase 'וכתב לה'.

steps.title: Divorce happens only through writing, not through money
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn from 'וכתב לה' that a woman is divorced only by a written גט. Without this, we might have said that divorce, like קידושין, can be done with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is needed to teach: she is divorced by writing, and she is not divorced by money. You might have thought: since leaving a marriage is compared to entering a marriage, then just as entering a marriage can be done with money, leaving it can also be done with money. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן need 'וכתב לה' for a different rule: a divorce must be done by writing, never by giving money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה links leaving a marriage (יציאה) to entering a marriage (הויה), and קידושין can be done with money. Because of that link, we might have thought a man could also divorce his wife by giving her money. 'וכתב לה' blocks that idea: only writing works.

keyTerms.meaning: She is divorced through writing (a written גט)
It might have entered your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)
Was compared or linked (a הקש, a comparison set up by the פסוק)
Leaving, meaning ending a marriage through divorce
Becoming, meaning entering a marriage through קידושין
It teaches us (the תורה tells us the opposite of the first thought)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lessons. רבי יוסי הגלילי used 'וכתב לה' for WHAT a גט may be written on. The רבנן use it for HOW a divorce happens: by writing and not by money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic halacha that a marriage can only be ended with a written גט, never with money.

phrases.english: That phrase is needed for it:
she is divorced by writing,
and she is not divorced by money.
It might have entered your mind to say:
since leaving a marriage is compared to entering a marriage,
just as entering a marriage can be done with money,
so too leaving a marriage can be done with money.
phrases.notes: This is the mistaken first thought (סלקא דעתך).

phrases.english: So the verse teaches us that it cannot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by giving the רבנן a separate lesson from 'וכתב לה'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use 'וכתב לה' to teach that a divorce happens only through writing and not through money, even though יציאה is compared to הויה.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי הגלילי learn that money cannot divorce?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי הגלילי used 'וכתב לה' for a different lesson, the גמרא asks where he learns that divorce cannot be done with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי, where does he learn this idea, that a woman cannot be divorced with money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יוסי הגלילי and asks for his source for the 'no divorce by money' rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי already used 'וכתב לה' to teach that a גט can be written on anything. So he cannot also use it for the rule that money does not divorce. Yet everyone agrees to that rule, so he must have another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Idea or reasoning (here, the rule that money cannot divorce)
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
from where does he learn this idea?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of step 8 around: now רבי יוסי הגלילי needs a source for the lesson the רבנן took from 'וכתב לה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי הגלילי's source for the rule that a woman is not divorced with money.

steps.title: A written document cuts the marriage, and nothing else does
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from 'ספר כריתות' that only a written document ends the marriage, and nothing else, including money.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'a scroll of cutting off': a scroll (a written document) cuts her off from her husband, and nothing else cuts her off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי gets the 'no money' rule from the words 'ספר כריתות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'ספר כריתות' to mean that the document is the thing that does the cutting. The message is 'only a ספר'. That rules out money or any other method of divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it (it comes out for him) from
'A scroll of cutting off', the תורה's name for a גט
Cuts her off (ends her marriage)

phrases.english: He derives it from 'a scroll of severance':
a scroll cuts her off,
and nothing else cuts her off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 with a different פסוק phrase for רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from 'ספר כריתות' that only a written document, and nothing else, ends the marriage.

steps.title: The רבנן need 'ספר כריתות' for full separation
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן cannot use 'ספר כריתות' for the 'no money' rule, because they need it to teach that a גט must completely cut the connection between husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן need this phrase 'a scroll of cutting off' for something else: the גט must be something that fully cuts the connection between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן do not learn the 'no money' rule from 'ספר כריתות'. They need those words for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not ask a question out loud here. It is understood: why don't the רבנן use 'ספר כריתות' like רבי יוסי הגלילי does? The answer is that they use it to require a complete break. A גט that still leaves the husband with some lasting hold over his wife does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (another lesson)
Something that cuts off completely
Between him and her

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this phrase 'a scroll of severance'

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְדָבָר הַכּוֹרֵת בֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ.
phrases.english: is needed for teaching that it must be something that cuts between him and her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the רבנן do not read 'ספר כריתות' the way רבי יוסי הגלילי does in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use 'ספר כריתות' to require that a גט fully cut the bond between husband and wife.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows which conditions block a full break
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows what 'complete cutting off' means. A גט given on condition that the wife never drinks wine, or never visits her father's house, is not a real cutting off. The same condition for only thirty days is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if a man says, 'This is your גט on condition that you never drink wine,' or 'on condition that you never go to your father's house,' that is not a cutting off. If the condition is only for thirty days, that is a cutting off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as an example of the רבנן's lesson from step 12. It shows exactly what a 'complete break' looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition that lasts forever ties the wife to her husband's demand for her whole life. The bond never fully ends, so the גט is not valid. A condition that lasts a limited time, like thirty days, runs out, and then the break is complete, so the גט works.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
This is your גט
On condition that
Forever, with no end date

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the condition itself. Conditions on a גט are allowed. The problem is a condition with NO end date, which keeps her tied to him forever.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, 'ספר כריתות' means a גט must end the bond completely. A condition with no end date makes the גט invalid. A time-limited condition, such as thirty days, is fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical halacha about conditional גיטין: a condition may not leave the woman permanently bound to her husband.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
'This is your bill of divorce'
on condition that you do not drink wine,

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא תֵּלְכִי לְבֵית אָבִיךְ לְעוֹלָם —
phrases.english: or on condition that you never go to your father's house, ever,
phrases.notes: 'Forever' applies to both conditions.

phrases.english: that is not severance.
If it is for thirty days only,
that is severance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the רבנן's lesson from step 12 with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט with a lifelong condition is not 'כריתות' and is invalid. A גט with a time-limited condition (such as thirty days) is valid.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns full separation from the longer word
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי also accepts the full-break rule. He learns it from the fact that the תורה wrote the longer word 'כריתות' instead of the shorter 'כרת', so the phrase teaches two lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי learns it from the difference between 'כרת' and 'כריתות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבי יוסי הגלילי learns that a גט must fully cut the bond. He uses the extra letters in the word 'כריתות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have used the short word 'כרת' but wrote the longer 'כריתות'. The extra letters show that the phrase teaches two things. רבי יוסי הגלילי uses one for 'only a document divorces, not money' and the other for 'the break must be complete'. So he reaches the same two rules about how a גט works as the רבנן, just from different words. The two sides still disagree about whether a גט may be written on a living thing or on food. The next step explains why the רבנן do not read 'כריתות' this way.

keyTerms.meaning: The short form of the word 'cut off'
The longer form, which the תורה actually wrote; its extra letters teach an extra lesson

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on two rules: a גט works only through writing and not with money, and it must fully end the bond. They disagree about which words teach these rules, and about whether a גט may be written on a living thing or on food.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
derives it from the fact that it says 'keritut' rather than 'karet'.
phrases.notes: The longer word teaches an extra lesson.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״כָּרֵת״ ״כְּרִיתוּת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question: since רבי יוסי הגלילי used 'ספר כריתות' for the 'no money' rule, where does he learn the full-break rule from steps 12-13?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The longer form 'כריתות' (instead of 'כרת') lets רבי יוסי הגלילי learn both the 'no money' rule and the full-break rule from the same phrase.

steps.title: The רבנן do not learn from the longer word
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not learn anything from the difference between 'כרת' and 'כריתות'. So they need the whole phrase 'ספר כריתות' for the full-break rule, and they must learn 'no money' from somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן do not learn anything from the difference between 'כרת' and 'כריתות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן cannot use the extra letters, as רבי יוסי הגלילי did. This closes the side discussion about how a גט works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14, רבי יוסי הגלילי got two lessons from 'ספר כריתות' because the תורה wrote the longer word instead of 'כרת'. The רבנן do not treat the longer form as extra, so the phrase gives them only one lesson: the full break. That is why they learn 'no money' from 'וכתב לה' instead.

keyTerms.meaning: The short form: 'cutting off'
The longer form of the same word, used in the פסוק
They do not learn a lesson from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי: 'וכתב לה' teaches a separate lesson. 'ספר כריתות' teaches both 'only a document, not money' and 'a full break', because of the long word כריתות. רבנן: 'וכתב לה' teaches 'not money'. 'ספר כריתות' teaches only the full break, because they do not learn from כרת versus כריתות.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, 'karet' versus 'keritut',
do not derive anything from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the method used by רבי יוסי הגלילי in Step 14 is not available to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why don't the רבנן also get two lessons out of 'ספר כריתות'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They do not treat the longer word כריתות as a source for an extra lesson.

steps.title: A caravan may fence itself in with animal equipment
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a caravan camping in an open valley may surround itself with a fence made of animal equipment and carry inside. The fence must be ten טפחים high, and the gaps may not be more than the built parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a caravan camped in a valley and surrounded itself with animal equipment, people may carry inside. The fence must be ten טפחים high, and the gaps may not be more than the built parts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a temporary fence made of saddles and similar gear can turn an open field into a private area for carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A valley is normally a כרמלית, where carrying is not allowed. A fence turns the area into an enclosed space. The משנה gives two conditions: the fence must be ten טפחים tall, and the open parts may not be more than the standing parts.

keyTerms.meaning: A caravan of travelers
A valley; an open field with no walls
Animal equipment, like saddles and packs
They may carry objects
Breaches; gaps in the fence
The built (standing) part of the fence

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic rule of מחיצות: a fence still counts even if it has gaps, as long as the built parts are not outnumbered by the open parts.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A caravan that camped in a valley
and they surrounded it with animal equipment —
one may carry inside it.
Provided that there is a fence
ten handbreadths high,
and that the breaches are not
more than the built part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the side discussion about גט ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fence of animal equipment allows carrying if it is ten טפחים high and its gaps are not more than its built parts.

steps.title: A gap of up to ten cubits counts as an entrance
steps.stepSummary: Any single gap of about ten אמות is allowed because it counts as an entrance. A gap wider than that forbids carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any gap of about ten אמות is allowed, because it counts as an entrance. If a gap is wider than that, carrying is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second limit: besides the overall count of open versus built, no single gap may be wider than ten אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A narrow opening looks like a doorway, and a doorway is a normal part of an enclosure, so it does not break the fence. A gap wider than ten אמות no longer looks like a doorway. It is a real hole, and it ruins the whole enclosure.

keyTerms.meaning: Cubits (an אמה is about 18-24 inches)
Like an entrance or doorway
More than this amount

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate rules here. First, all the gaps together may not be more than the built parts (Step 16). Second, no single gap may be wider than ten אמות. A fence must pass both tests.

phrases.english: Any breach that is
about ten cubits is permitted,
because it is like an entrance.
More than this — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל פִּירְצָה שֶׁהִיא כְּעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת מוּתֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to the fence rules of Step 16, this time about the size of one single gap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gap of up to ten אמות counts as an entrance and is allowed. A wider gap forbids carrying.

steps.title: Dispute: a fence whose gaps exactly equal its built parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a disagreement about a fence where the open parts exactly equal the built parts. רב פפא permits carrying, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated that the אמוראים disagree about a fence whose gaps exactly equal its built parts. רב פפא said: it is permitted. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a disagreement about a case the משנה left unclear: exactly half open and half built. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said the gaps may not be 'more than' the built parts, so an exactly equal fence is not clearly covered. רב פפא reads it as: only more is a problem, so equal is fine. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds that the built parts must be the majority, so equal is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The open part equals the standing part
Permitted
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: 'פרוץ כעומד' does not mean 'mostly open'. It means exactly equal: half gap, half fence. That in-between case is the only thing being argued about.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was stated: breached equal to standing —
Rav Pappa said: it is permitted,
Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,
said: it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'not more than the built part' rule from Step 16 and asks what happens in the exactly equal case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא permits carrying in a fence that is exactly half open. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע forbids it.

steps.title: רב פפא permits carrying: just do not break open most of the fence
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says a fence whose gaps equal its built parts is valid, because the rule given to משה only forbids a fence that is mostly broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is permitted. This is how the Merciful One taught משה: do not break open the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the reason for רב פפא's opinion from step 18. He permits carrying when the open parts equal the built parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא says the rule from סיני was framed as a prohibition: 'do not break open most of it.' At exactly half-and-half, the broken part is not 'most,' so the fence is still valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted
The Merciful One (ה׳) taught משה, meaning a הלכה למשה מסיני
Do not break open
Its majority, most of it

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that 'most' is the key. They disagree only about which side needs to be the majority. At exactly 50/50 that makes all the difference.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is permitted.
This is how the Merciful One taught Moses:
phrases.notes: A tradition from סיני about partitions.

phrases.english: Do not break open the majority (of the fence).
phrases.notes: Only a fence that is mostly broken is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reasoning for רב פפא's ruling introduced in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gaps equal to the built parts are permitted, since the fence is not mostly broken.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע forbids carrying: most of it must be fenced
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the rule given to משה requires that most of the area be fenced in, so half-and-half is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: It is forbidden. This is how the Merciful One taught משה: fence in the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposing reason. רב הונא forbids carrying when the open and built parts are equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads the same tradition as a positive requirement: 'fence in most of it.' At exactly half-and-half, the built part is not 'most,' so the fence fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden
Fence in, enclose

steps.whyThisMatters: The two opinions are mirror images. One requires that the broken part not be the majority. The other requires that the built part be the majority. They differ only in the exact 50/50 case.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר אָסוּר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said: It is forbidden.
This is how the Merciful One taught Moses:
Fence in the majority.
phrases.notes: The built part must be more than half.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing side of the disagreement, with its reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gaps equal to the built parts are forbidden, since most of the area is not fenced in.

steps.title: The משנה's wording seems to permit equal gaps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, 'the gaps may not be more than the built parts,' and infers that equal gaps are permitted. This contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'The gaps may not be more than the built parts.' That implies that if they are equal to the built parts, it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע using the exact words of the משנה from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only forbids gaps that are 'more than' the built parts. By inference, gaps that are exactly equal should be fine. That matches רב פפא and goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaches, gaps
The built (standing) part of the fence
This implies (an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: We learned: And the gaps may not be
more than the built part.
This implies: if they equal the built part, it is permitted?!
phrases.notes: A challenge to רב הונא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְלֹא יְהוּ פִּירְצוֹת יְתֵרוֹת עַל הַבִּנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion stated in step 20 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ruling that equal gaps are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inference from the משנה's phrase 'more than the built part': only 'more than' is forbidden, so 'equal' is allowed.

steps.title: Reread the משנה: it is permitted only when the built part is more
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב הונא by reading the משנה's inference differently: permission comes only when the built part is greater than the gaps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'if equal to the built part, it is permitted.' Instead say: 'if the built part is more than the gap, it is permitted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save רב הונא's opinion by changing which inference we draw from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposal is that the משנה's point is that the built part must be greater. On this reading, the equal case is not automatically permitted, so רב הונא can still forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say... rather say (a rereading)
More, greater

phrases.english: Do not say: 'If equal to the built part, it is permitted,'
rather say:

phrases.aramaic: אִם בִּנְיָן יָתֵר עַל הַפִּירְצָה — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: If the built part is more than the gap, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא הָא כַּבִּנְיָן מוּתָּר, אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 on behalf of רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the inference drawn from the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies that equal gaps are permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה implies only that a greater built part is permitted, so the equal case may be forbidden.

steps.title: If equal were forbidden, the משנה should have said so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the rereading. If equal gaps are forbidden, the משנה should have said 'the gaps may not equal the built part.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they are equal to the built part, what is the law, forbidden? If so, the משנה should have taught: 'the gaps may not be equal to the built part'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 22 and shows it does not fit the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If equal gaps were forbidden, the clearest wording would be 'not equal to the built part.' That wording would also teach, all the more so, that more gaps are forbidden. Since the משנה chose 'more than,' it seems to allow the equal case.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let it teach (the משנה should have said)

phrases.english: But if equal to the built part, what is the law? Forbidden?
If so, let the משנה teach:
'The gaps may not be equal to the built part'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל כַּבִּנְיָן, מַאי — אָסוּר? אִי הָכִי לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The rereading of the משנה offered on behalf of רב הונא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה would have used the more precise wording 'not equal' if equal gaps were forbidden.

steps.title: The challenge to רב הונא stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes 'קשיא': the challenge against רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע remains unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by admitting that רב הונא's opinion has an unresolved problem from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' is not a full refutation. It means the question stands without an answer. Still, the plain reading of the משנה supports רב פפא, who permits equal gaps.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty, an unresolved challenge

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא: 'do not break open most of it,' so equal gaps are permitted. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: 'fence in most of it,' so equal gaps are forbidden. The משנה's wording ('gaps not more than the built part') fits רב פפא, and the challenge to רב הונא is left as a קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' does not mean 'תיובתא' (a full refutation). It means the opinion has a difficulty that was not resolved.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the back-and-forth of steps 21-23 by leaving the challenge unresolved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's wording poses an unanswered difficulty for רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, and the plain reading supports רב פפא.

steps.title: A proof from skewers used as סוכה roofing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if someone roofs his סוכה with metal skewers or bed-frame poles, and the gaps between them equal their width, the סוכה is כשירה. This seems to show that 'equal' is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who roofs his סוכה with skewers or with the long poles of a bed, if there is space between them equal to their width, the סוכה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a משנה from the laws of סוכה, to show that half-and-half counts as valid. This supports רב פפא and works against רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skewers and bed poles cannot be used as סכך, so they are the 'bad' part, and the valid סכך in the gaps is the 'good' part. The משנה says the gaps are כמותן, 'like them,' meaning equal, and still the סוכה is כשירה. If equal works for סכך, then equal should also work for a wall that is half built and half open.

keyTerms.meaning: One who puts a roof on (here, covers the סוכה)
Metal skewers (cannot be used as סכך)
The long side poles of a bed frame
Empty space, gap
Like them, equal to their width

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא compares two different areas of הלכה, סכך on a סוכה and walls for שבת, because both raise the same question: does an equal amount of 'good' and 'bad' count as good?

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to quote a source.

phrases.english: One who roofs his sukka with skewers
phrases.notes: Metal skewers can become טמא, so they are invalid as סכך

phrases.english: or with the long poles of a bed,
phrases.notes: Also invalid for סכך

phrases.english: if there is space between them equal to them —
phrases.notes: The gaps are filled with valid סכך

phrases.english: it is valid!
phrases.notes: This is the key word for the proof

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (it also attacks רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קשיא in step 24 was left unanswered, the גמרא brings a further source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's view that an equal split, with the built part equal to the open part, is valid (against רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה about roofing with skewers or bed poles that have gaps כמותן

steps.title: The gaps are a bit wider so the skewers can slide in and out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof: the משנה is talking about gaps a little wider than the skewers, so the skewers can be put in and taken out easily. That means the valid סכך is actually more than the invalid part.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what are we dealing here? With a case where the skewers go in and come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by saying the משנה is not really describing an exactly equal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the gap were exactly the width of a skewer, a skewer would be jammed tight. The משנה pictures gaps loose enough that a skewer can slide in and out freely, so the valid space is slightly bigger. In that case the good part is the majority, which fits רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? The גמרא is limiting a source to a specific situation
Goes in and comes out, meaning it fits loosely

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the סוכה is invalid. It agrees the סוכה is כשירה, but says that is because the gaps are slightly MORE than the skewers, not exactly equal.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to explain the source as talking about one specific case.

phrases.english: Where it goes in and comes out.
phrases.notes: The skewer fits loosely, so the gap is a bit wider than the skewer

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תירוץ (defending רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 25 by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; the משנה's ruling that the סוכה is כשירה stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed כמותן means exactly equal, but the case may have gaps slightly larger than the skewers.

steps.title: But exact measuring is possible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the deflection: it is possible to make the gaps exactly equal, so why not read the משנה as an exactly equal case?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it possible to be precise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It says the משנה could really be describing gaps that are exactly equal to the skewers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deflection depended on the idea that the gaps must be a little wider. But a person can measure carefully and make the gaps exactly equal, and כמותן sounds like exactly equal. So the proof for רב פפא seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, a word that opens a challenge
To be exact, to measure precisely

phrases.english: But isn't it possible to be precise?
phrases.notes: So the משנה could still mean exactly equal gaps

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case definition offered in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The deflection in step 26 that the gaps are wider so the skewers slide in and out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exact equality can be achieved, and the משנה's word כמותן fits an exact match, so the משנה may still show that equal is valid.

steps.title: רבי אמי: extra valid roofing was added
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the person added extra valid סכך, so the good part is more than the bad part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: It is a case where he adds.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question to save the deflection: in the משנה's case, more valid סכך was added, so it is not an exactly equal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if precise measuring is possible, the משנה is read as a case where the valid סכך goes beyond the skewers' width. So the סוכה is כשירה because the good part is the majority, not because equal is enough. The proof for רב פפא is pushed away, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is not disproven from here.

keyTerms.meaning: Adds extra, making one side more than the other

steps.whatToRemember: The סוכה משנה does not prove that half-and-half is valid. According to רבי אמי, it describes a case where the valid סכך is more than the invalid skewers, so it fits the rule that most must be good.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Where he adds extra.
phrases.notes: The valid סכך is more than the skewers

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27 and so keeps step 26's rejection of the proof in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing (אוקימתא): the משנה refers to a case where valid roofing was added.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might describe gaps exactly equal to the skewers, which would prove that equal is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה describes a case where the valid סכך is greater, so it gives no proof that an exact equal split is valid.

steps.title: רבא: lay the valid roofing in the opposite direction from the skewers
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives another answer to the question in Step 27. In the משנה, the person laid valid סכך across the skewers in the opposite direction, so the valid part ends up being more than the invalid part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If the skewers were placed crosswise, he places the valid roofing lengthwise. If the skewers were placed lengthwise, he places the valid roofing crosswise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different way to answer the question from Step 27. It is a second answer, alongside the one from רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 asked why we don't read the משנה as a case where the gaps are exactly equal. רבא answers that the valid סכך is laid in the opposite direction from the skewers, so it lies across them. This way the valid סכך covers the skewers' area too, and the good part becomes more than the bad part.

keyTerms.meaning: Crosswise (borrowed from weaving: the threads that run across)
Lengthwise (borrowed from weaving: the threads that run the long way)
Placed / laid down
He places it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is disagreeing about the law. Like רבי אמי, he agrees the משנה must be talking about a case where valid סכך is more than invalid. He only explains a different way the person could arrange it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If they (the skewers) were placed crosswise —
phrases.notes: עֵרֶב and שְׁתִי are weaving terms for the two directions of threads.

phrases.english: he places it (the valid roofing) lengthwise;
if lengthwise — he places it crosswise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אִם הָיוּ נְתוּנִין עֵרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question in Step 27, alongside רבי אמי's answer in Step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about valid סכך laid across the skewers in the opposite direction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could be read as a case where the gaps are exactly equal to the skewers, which would prove that 'equal' is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about valid סכך laid in the opposite direction from the skewers, so valid is more than invalid. The משנה does not prove that 'equal' is enough.

steps.title: A new proof begins: a caravan surrounded by camels and saddles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new proof from a ברייתא about a caravan that camped in a valley and surrounded itself with camels and saddles. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A caravan that camped in a valley and surrounded it with camels, with saddles,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof by starting to quote a ברייתא. This passage ends before the ruling, so the actual proof comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תא שמע' tells us a new source is being brought in to test the question of פרוץ כעומד. A caravan using camels and saddles as a makeshift wall raises the same issue: how much open space is allowed between the parts of a partition. The גמרא brings this source to try to support the view of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: A caravan of travelers
A valley / open field (a כרמלית, not a private domain)
Camels
Saddles

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A caravan that camped in a valley
and they surrounded it with camels, with saddles,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the skewer proof from Steps 25-29 was answered, the גמרא brings a new source to test the same question.
steps.raayaObject: The status of a partition that is exactly half open and half closed (פרוץ כעומד), connected to the view of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a caravan in a valley surrounding its camp with camels and saddles (the quote continues on the next amud)
